examNote: 80% pass mark is confirmed (DMV help pages, sa.dmv.ca.gov ruleid 2913/2914). DMV does not publish the question count; 36 for adults (46/38 for minors) is UNVERIFIED and must be confirmed before release.

questions.q: What must you do when you reach this sign?
options: Slow down and keep going if no cars are coming
Stop only if another vehicle is already in the intersection
Come to a full stop, then go only when it is safe
questions.explain: A STOP sign always requires a complete stop at the limit line, the crosswalk, or the edge of the cross street, and you may go only after yielding to traffic that is close enough to be a hazard.

questions.q: What does this sign require you to do?
options: Stop completely every time, even when the road is clear
Speed up to merge ahead of cross traffic
Slow down, stop if needed, and let nearby traffic go first
questions.explain: At a YIELD sign you must give the right-of-way to vehicles already in the intersection or close enough to be a hazard, stopping only when necessary.

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: You may not drive into this road from your direction
The road ahead is closed to trucks only
You must stop and then enter carefully
questions.explain: The DO NOT ENTER sign is placed where traffic from your direction is not allowed, such as the wrong end of a one-way road or a freeway exit ramp.

questions.q: What does this sign tell you about the street?
options: Only one lane is open ahead
Turning is allowed only in the arrow's direction during rush hour
All traffic on this street moves only in the direction of the arrow
questions.explain: A ONE WAY sign marks a roadway where vehicles may travel in just one direction, and California law requires you to drive only in that direction.

questions.q: At an intersection posted with this sign, which move is not allowed?
options: Turning left
Going straight
Making a U-turn
questions.explain: The red circle and slash over a U-shaped arrow is a movement prohibition sign that bans U-turns at that location.

questions.q: What does this sign prohibit?
options: Left turns
Right turns
Changing lanes to the left
questions.explain: A black left-turn arrow inside a red circle with a slash means left turns are not permitted at that intersection.

questions.q: You are stopped at a red light and see this sign. What does it mean?
options: You may turn right on red without stopping first
You may turn on red only if no pedestrians are present
You must wait for a green light before turning
questions.explain: California normally allows a turn on red after a full stop, but this sign takes that option away, so you must wait for a signal that allows the turn.

questions.q: What does this five-sided sign warn you about?
options: A school area where children may be present
A playground inside a park
A pedestrian bridge overhead
questions.explain: The upward-pointing pentagon shape is reserved for the School sign, which warns that you are approaching a school area or school zone.

questions.q: What does this sign mark?
options: A four-way stop
A railroad crossing where you must yield to trains
A detour around a closed road
questions.explain: The X-shaped Crossbuck marks a highway-rail crossing; you must yield to trains and stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail when a train is coming.

questions.q: What does this round yellow sign warn you about?
options: A traffic circle ahead
A road that is closed ahead
A railroad crossing ahead
questions.explain: The circular yellow sign with an X and two R letters is the advance warning sign for a railroad crossing; the circle shape is used only for this sign.

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: The road ahead curves to the right
You must turn right at the next street
Right lane ends ahead
questions.explain: A curved arrow on a yellow diamond is a horizontal alignment warning that the road bends in the direction shown, so adjust your speed before the curve.

questions.q: What should you expect after passing this sign?
options: A divided highway begins
The road becomes one-way
Vehicles from another roadway may move into your lane
questions.explain: The Merge sign warns that traffic from a joining roadway will be entering the same lane ahead, so watch for merging vehicles and adjust your speed or position.

questions.q: You are driving in the right lane and see this sign. What does it mean?
options: The number of lanes is reduced ahead, so prepare to merge left
A bike lane begins on the right
Traffic from the right does not stop
questions.explain: The Lane Ends sign warns that one lane is ending and the number of lanes in your direction will drop, so drivers in the ending lane must merge.

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: A railroad crossing with lights ahead
A traffic signal ahead that may be hard to see
A police checkpoint ahead
questions.explain: The Signal Ahead sign is posted before a traffic signal that you cannot see from far enough away, giving you time to prepare to stop.

questions.q: What does this sign tell you?
options: Two lanes in your direction ahead
Divided highway begins
Oncoming traffic will share the road ahead
questions.explain: The Two-Way Traffic sign warns that the road changes to a section where traffic travels in both directions, so expect oncoming vehicles.

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: A divided highway begins, with a median separating opposing traffic
The road narrows to one lane
A fork in the road where you must choose left or right
questions.explain: The Divided Highway sign warns that a median will separate the two directions; in California you must stay to the right of the median and may not drive across it.

questions.q: What should you do when you see this sign?
options: Honk to warn people walking nearby
Watch for people crossing and be ready to yield
Speed up to clear the area quickly
questions.explain: This warning sign alerts you to a place where pedestrians may cross the road, so slow down and be prepared to let them cross.

questions.q: What does this sign require?
options: Pass to the right of the island or obstruction ahead
Use only the left lane ahead
Turn right at the next intersection
questions.explain: The Keep Right sign is used where traffic must pass only on the right side of a median, island, or other obstruction.

questions.q: What does this white rectangular sign mean?
options: Passing is allowed with care
Slower traffic must keep right
You may not pass other vehicles in this area
questions.explain: DO NOT PASS is a regulatory sign used where passing is unsafe, such as where sight distance is limited, and it must be obeyed.

questions.q: This pennant-shaped sign is placed on the left side of the road. What does it tell you?
options: Passing lane begins
Road narrows ahead
A no-passing zone begins here
questions.explain: The pennant shape is reserved for the NO PASSING ZONE sign, which is mounted on the left side of the road at the start of a no-passing zone.

questions.q: What does the orange color of this sign tell you?
options: A recreation area is ahead
There is a hospital nearby
There is a temporary work zone ahead
questions.explain: Orange is the color for temporary traffic control, so this sign warns of road work ahead where you should slow down and watch for workers and equipment.

questions.q: You see this sign while driving on a California highway. What does it mean?
options: On a green ball you may turn left, but you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
You may turn left only on a green arrow
Oncoming traffic must stop to let you turn left
questions.explain: This sign means left turns are allowed on a circular green light, but turning drivers must first yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.q: What does this sign over or beside a freeway lane mean?
options: The lane is for trucks only
The lane is reserved for vehicles carrying at least two people during its posted hours
The lane is a toll lane for all vehicles
questions.explain: The white diamond marks a high-occupancy vehicle lane; the 2+ means a vehicle needs at least two occupants, and drivers must follow the posted rules for that lane.

questions.q: In California, a vehicle displaying this emblem on its rear is one that:
options: Is carrying hazardous materials
Is an emergency vehicle
Is designed to travel at 25 mph or less
questions.explain: California requires the orange triangle with a red reflective border on vehicles designed to be operated at 25 mph or less, so expect it to be moving much slower than traffic.

questions.q: What does this blue sign tell you?
options: A hospital is nearby
Helicopters land here
Hazardous road ahead
questions.explain: Blue signs give road-user service information; the white H means a hospital is available nearby.

questions.q: Which sign warns that you will reach a STOP sign ahead?
questions.explain: The Stop Ahead sign shows a small stop sign with an arrow and is used when the STOP sign itself cannot be seen early enough.

questions.q: Which sign warns that the road may be slippery when it is wet?
questions.explain: The car with skid marks is the Slippery When Wet sign, which warns of surfaces that can lose traction, especially in rain.

questions.q: Which sign tells you that you are driving against the flow of traffic and must not continue?
questions.explain: The red WRONG WAY sign faces drivers who have entered a one-way road or ramp in the wrong direction, so stop going forward and leave safely.

questions.q: What background color is used on signs for temporary road work zones?
questions.explain: Work zone (temporary traffic control) warning signs have black legends on an orange background.

questions.q: What background color do standard warning signs, such as a curve warning, use?
questions.explain: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped with a black symbol or message on a yellow background.

questions.q: Warning signs for schools and school buses use which background color?
questions.explain: School and school bus warning signs must have a black legend on a fluorescent yellow-green background so they stand out.

questions.q: On traffic signs, which color generally means stop or that something is prohibited?
questions.explain: Under the national color code, red is used for stop and for prohibitions, such as the slash on a no-turn sign.

questions.q: Signs that guide you to parks and other recreational or cultural areas use which background color?
questions.explain: Brown is reserved for recreational and cultural interest area guidance, while blue is used for road-user services.

questions.q: An eight-sided (octagon) sign is used for which sign only?
options: YIELD
Railroad crossing ahead
STOP
questions.explain: The octagon shape is reserved exclusively for the STOP sign so drivers can recognize it even from behind or when it is covered with snow or dirt.

questions.q: A sign shaped like a triangle pointing downward always means:
options: Yield
Warning of a hill
No passing
questions.explain: The downward-pointing equilateral triangle is used only for the YIELD sign.

questions.q: A round (circular) warning sign is used only to warn of:
options: A roundabout ahead
A school crossing
A railroad crossing ahead
questions.explain: The circle shape is limited to the Grade Crossing Advance Warning sign, which tells you a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.q: What does a diamond-shaped sign usually tell you?
options: It gives directions to a city
It warns of a possible hazard or change in the road ahead
It shows a legal speed limit
questions.explain: Warning signs are normally diamond-shaped and alert you to conditions such as curves, merges, or crossings ahead.

questions.q: Signs that tell you a traffic law, such as a speed limit or turn restriction, are usually:
options: Rectangles with black or red on a white background
Diamonds with black on yellow
Pentagons with black on green
questions.explain: Regulatory signs are rectangular unless another shape is specified, and white is the color code for regulation.

questions.q: What must you do at a flashing red traffic light?
options: Slow down and go through without stopping
Stop only if cross traffic is present
Stop completely, then go when it is safe, just as at a STOP sign
questions.explain: California treats a flashing red light like a STOP sign: stop at the limit line or crosswalk, then proceed under the usual stop-sign rules.

questions.q: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: Stop and wait for green
Continue through carefully, watching for hazards
The signal is about to turn green
questions.explain: A flashing yellow light lets you proceed through the intersection, but only with caution.

questions.q: A steady yellow traffic light means:
options: The green signal is ending and a red light is coming next
You must speed up to beat the red
You may turn but not go straight
questions.explain: A steady yellow warns drivers that the green movement is ending and the signal will turn red right after.

questions.q: At a steady red light with no sign prohibiting it, may you turn right?
options: No, never on a red light
Yes, without stopping if the way is clear
Yes, after a full stop and yielding to pedestrians and nearby traffic
questions.explain: California allows a right turn on a steady red after stopping, unless a sign forbids it, and you must yield to pedestrians and close traffic.

questions.q: You are in a left-turn lane facing a green left arrow and no sign prohibits U-turns. Which move is allowed?
options: Only going straight
A left turn or a U-turn, while yielding to pedestrians in the crosswalk
Only a right turn
questions.explain: A green arrow allows the movement it shows, and in California a left green arrow also permits a U-turn unless a sign prohibits it; you still yield to pedestrians and other lawful traffic.

questions.q: Lane-use control lights hang over each lane of a road. What does a steady red signal over a lane mean?
options: You may use that lane only to pass
You may not drive in that lane
You may use that lane only to turn left
questions.explain: A steady red lane-control signal means you must not enter or travel in that lane; a flashing yellow one allows the lane only for left turns.

questions.q: A yellow curve warning sign has a small plaque below it showing "25 MPH." What does the plaque mean?
options: It is the recommended safe speed for the curve
It is the minimum speed allowed on the curve
It is the speed limit for trucks only
questions.explain: An Advisory Speed plaque under a warning sign shows the recommended speed for the condition ahead, such as a sharp curve.

questions.q: Unless a higher limit is posted under state law, the maximum speed on California highways is ___ mph.
questions.explain: California sets a general maximum of 65 mph; 70 mph applies only on highways posted for it.

questions.q: On a two-lane, undivided California highway, the maximum speed is ___ mph unless a higher speed is posted.
questions.explain: A highway with only one through lane each way and no divider has a 55 mph maximum unless signs allow more.

questions.q: On California highways where it is posted, the highest legal speed limit is ___ mph.
questions.explain: Caltrans, with CHP approval, may raise the limit to 70 mph on certain highways, and no one may exceed 70 mph there.

questions.q: When you drive a passenger vehicle that is pulling a trailer in California, you may not drive faster than ___ mph.
questions.explain: California limits passenger vehicles towing another vehicle to 55 mph, even where the posted limit is higher.

questions.q: In a business or residence district, unless signs show a different limit, the speed limit is ___ mph.
questions.explain: The prima facie limit in business and residence districts is 25 mph unless a different limit is set and posted.

questions.q: The speed limit in an alley in California is ___ mph.
questions.explain: California law sets a 15 mph prima facie limit on any alley.

questions.q: When you pass a school posted with a SCHOOL warning sign while children are going to or leaving school, the speed limit is ___ mph unless a different limit is posted.
questions.explain: The standard school limit is 25 mph near schools with a SCHOOL sign while children are arriving, leaving, or at noon recess, unless a local limit is posted.

questions.q: In California, driving faster than ___ mph is a separate offense that can lead to a fine and a license suspension.
questions.explain: Driving over 100 mph carries its own penalties, including fines and possible suspension of your driving privilege.

questions.q: What does California's basic speed law require?
options: Always driving exactly at the posted limit
Never driving faster than is safe for current conditions
Keeping up with the fastest traffic
questions.explain: The basic speed law forbids driving faster than is reasonable and prudent for the conditions, and never at a speed that endangers people or property.

questions.q: Under the basic speed law, which conditions must you consider when choosing your speed?
options: Only the posted speed limit
Only the time of day and your car's top speed
Weather, visibility, traffic, and the road's surface and width
questions.explain: The law lists weather, visibility, traffic, and the surface and width of the road as factors in deciding what speed is safe.

questions.q: Thick fog cuts your view to a short distance on a freeway posted at 65 mph. If you drive 65 mph, you:
options: Could be cited because your speed is unsafe for the conditions
Are always legal because you are at the posted limit
Are legal as long as your headlights are on
questions.explain: Even at or below the posted limit, you violate the basic speed law if your speed is too fast for poor visibility.

questions.q: California calls many of its speed limits "prima facie" limits. What does driving faster than a prima facie limit mean?
options: It is always legal if no crash occurs
It applies only at night
It is presumed unlawful unless you can show the speed was safe for the conditions
questions.explain: Exceeding a prima facie limit is presumed to violate the basic speed law, but the driver may try to prove the speed was safe at that time and place.

questions.q: You drove 72 mph on a highway with a 65 mph maximum limit, in clear weather and light traffic. Can you avoid a violation by showing your speed was safe?
options: No, exceeding a maximum speed limit is a violation regardless
Yes, if traffic was light
Yes, if the road was dry
questions.explain: The 65 and 70 mph limits are absolute maximums; the safe-speed defense that applies to prima facie limits does not apply to them.

questions.q: Which of these vehicles is limited to 55 mph on California highways, even where the posted limit is 65 mph?
options: A motorcycle with a passenger
A pickup truck without a trailer
A school bus carrying students
questions.explain: State law caps school buses transporting pupils at 55 mph, along with towing vehicles, larger trucks, and some other vehicle types.

questions.q: You are pulling a trailer on a multi-lane highway with no lane designated for slower vehicles. Which lane should you normally use?
options: The far left lane
The right-hand lane, or as close to the right edge as practical
Any lane you like
questions.explain: Vehicles under the 55 mph rule, including those towing, must use a designated lane or, if none, the right-hand lane, moving left only to pass as the law allows.

questions.q: While towing a trailer on a divided highway with four or more marked lanes in your direction and no designated truck lane, which lanes may you use?
options: The right-hand lane or the lane immediately to its left
Only the far left lane
Only the shoulder
questions.explain: On divided highways with four or more lanes in one direction and no designated lane, towing vehicles may also use the lane just left of the right-hand lane.

questions.q: Is it legal to drive so slowly that you block the normal flow of traffic?
options: Yes, slow driving is always allowed
No, unless the slow speed is needed for safety, because of a grade, or to obey the law
Only on freeways
questions.explain: California prohibits driving so slowly that you impede normal and reasonable traffic, unless the slower speed is needed for safety, a grade, or legal compliance.

questions.q: A heavily loaded truck slows down while climbing a steep grade. Is the driver breaking the slow-driving law?
options: Yes, all vehicles must keep up with traffic
Yes, unless a police officer allows it
No, a reduced speed because of a grade is allowed
questions.explain: The law against impeding traffic makes an exception when the slower speed is caused by a grade or is necessary for safe operation.

questions.q: A speed limit sign has a plaque below it reading "MINIMUM 40." What does it mean?
options: You must not drive below 40 mph unless needed for safety
40 mph is the limit for trucks
You should drive 40 mph in bad weather
questions.explain: A minimum speed plaque shows the lowest legal speed on that road; California allows minimum limits where slow traffic blocks the normal flow, except when going slower is necessary for safety.

questions.q: Is it legal to stop your vehicle in a traffic lane and block normal traffic just to look at something?
options: Yes, if your hazard lights are on
No, stopping that blocks traffic is allowed only when needed for safety or required by law
Yes, for up to one minute
questions.explain: California forbids bringing a vehicle to a complete stop that blocks normal traffic unless the stop is necessary for safe operation or to obey the law.

questions.q: You approach an intersection with no stop signs, yield signs, or signals. In the last 100 feet you cannot see 100 feet down the cross streets. What is the speed limit?
options: 15 mph
25 mph
35 mph
questions.explain: At an uncontrolled intersection where your view of cross traffic is blocked, California sets a 15 mph prima facie limit.

questions.q: You are approaching a railroad crossing that has no gates, warning lights, or flagger. During the last 100 feet you cannot see 400 feet down the tracks in both directions. What is the speed limit?
options: 25 mph
20 mph
15 mph
questions.explain: When your view of the tracks is limited like this at a crossing without a flagger or signal device, the prima facie limit is 15 mph.

questions.q: What is the speed limit when passing a senior center posted with a "SENIOR" warning sign?
options: 15 mph
25 mph
35 mph
questions.explain: California sets a 25 mph prima facie limit when passing a senior center or similar facility posted with a SENIOR warning sign.

questions.q: When does the 25 mph school limit apply near a school posted with a SCHOOL sign?
options: Only during the first week of school
Any time of day, all year
While children are going to or leaving school during school hours or noon recess
questions.explain: The 25 mph school limit applies while children are arriving, leaving, or at noon recess, and when unfenced school grounds are being used by children.

questions.q: On a Saturday, children are playing on school grounds that have no fence next to the road, and the road is posted with a SCHOOL sign. What speed limit applies unless another limit is posted?
options: 25 mph
The normal limit, because it is not a school day
15 mph
questions.explain: The 25 mph school limit also applies when school grounds not separated from the road by a fence or barrier are in use by children and a SCHOOL sign is posted.

questions.q: Under California law, a standard SCHOOL warning sign may be placed up to how far from the school grounds?
options: 100 feet
500 feet
1,000 feet
questions.explain: The law allows standard SCHOOL warning signs to be placed at any distance up to 500 feet from school grounds.

questions.q: Near a school you see a posted school-zone speed limit of 20 mph or 15 mph. What should you do?
options: Ignore it, because the state school limit is always 25 mph
Obey only if a police officer is present
Obey the posted lower limit, since cities can lower school-zone limits
questions.explain: California lets local authorities set lower school-zone limits, such as 20 mph or, on some residential roads, 15 mph, once signs are posted.

questions.q: Highway workers are working next to the road in a zone posted with a reduced speed limit. Driving faster than the posted limit there is:
options: Presumed to violate the basic speed law
Legal if no workers are in your lane
Legal if you stay under the normal highway limit
questions.explain: Exceeding a properly posted work-zone limit where workers are endangered by traffic is prima facie a violation of the basic speed law.

questions.q: A sign on a bridge or in a tunnel posts a maximum speed for that structure. What must you do?
options: Ignore it if the general limit is higher
Drive no faster than the speed the structure can safely handle
Drive at least that speed to clear the bridge quickly
questions.explain: California prohibits driving on a bridge, elevated structure, tube, or tunnel faster than the speed it can safely handle, and posted signs are evidence of that maximum.

questions.q: If you are convicted for the first time of driving over 100 mph, the court may suspend your driving privilege for up to:
options: 30 days
6 months
1 year
questions.explain: A first conviction for exceeding 100 mph can bring a fine of up to $500 and a court-ordered suspension of up to 30 days.

questions.q: What happens if you are convicted of driving over 100 mph again within three years of an earlier conviction for the same offense?
options: Only a warning letter is sent
Your license is suspended by the DMV and a higher fine applies
Nothing more than the first time
questions.explain: A repeat over-100 mph conviction within three years raises the maximum fine and requires the DMV to suspend your driving privilege.

questions.q: A rural highway has one through lane in each direction, no median, and a few short passing lanes. If no higher limit is posted, what is the maximum speed?
options: 65 mph, because the passing lanes make it a four-lane road
70 mph
55 mph
questions.explain: Passing lanes do not count as through lanes, so the road is still a two-lane undivided highway with a 55 mph maximum unless posted higher.

questions.q: Some California freeways use electronic signs that show different speed limits at different times. Which limit must you follow?
options: The speed limit currently displayed on the sign
The lowest limit the sign has ever shown
The normal 65 mph limit, because electronic signs are only advice
questions.explain: Caltrans may install variable speed limit signs on freeways, and the limit displayed at the time applies to drivers.

questions.q: A winding road has sharp curves but no lowered speed limit sign. What does California law expect you to do?
options: Drive at the posted limit, since no lower limit is posted
Slow down as needed, because the basic speed law covers curves and other visible conditions
Drive at least 10 mph under the limit at all times
questions.explain: California relies on the basic speed law to handle obvious conditions like curves and grades, so you must choose a safe speed even without a special sign.

questions.q: You see this sign on a freeway while pulling a camping trailer behind your car. What is the fastest you may legally drive?
options: 65 mph
55 mph
60 mph
questions.explain: A passenger vehicle towing another vehicle is limited to 55 mph in California, even where the posted limit for other traffic is 65 mph.

questions.q: You (blue car) and the red car reach this all-way stop at the same moment. The red car is on your right. Who goes first?
options: You go first because you are going straight
Whoever honks first
The red car goes first
questions.explain: When two drivers arrive at an all-way stop together, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right, so the red car has the right-of-way.

questions.q: At an intersection with no signs or signals, another car has already entered the intersection from a cross street when you arrive. What should you do?
options: Yield to the car that is already in the intersection
Go first if you are on the wider street
Go first if the other car is on your left
questions.explain: A driver approaching an intersection must yield to any vehicle that has already entered it from a different road.

questions.q: You are on a road that ends at a T-intersection with a through road. There are no signs or signals. A car on the through road arrives at the same time as you. Who must yield?
options: The driver on the through road
Whichever driver is on the left
You, because your road ends there
questions.explain: At an uncontrolled intersection, a driver on a road that ends (does not continue past the intersection) must yield to traffic on the road that continues.

questions.q: You approach an intersection where the traffic lights are not working at all (completely dark). What must you do?
options: Stop, then go only when it is safe to do so
Slow down and continue if no one is coming
Keep the same speed because you have no signal to obey
questions.explain: When signals are inoperative, every driver must stop at the intersection and may proceed with caution only when it is safe.

questions.q: You (blue car) want to turn left on a green light. The red car is coming toward you and going straight. What should you do?
options: Wait and let the red car pass before turning
Turn quickly before the red car gets close
Turn because a green light gives you the right-of-way
questions.explain: A driver turning left must yield to oncoming vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard and keep yielding until the turn can be made safely.

questions.q: You are about to turn left from a street into a private driveway. An oncoming car is close enough to be a hazard. What does the law require?
options: You may turn because you signaled first
The oncoming car must stop for you
You must yield to the oncoming car until it is safe to turn
questions.explain: The left-turn yield rule also applies when turning into public or private property or an alley: oncoming traffic that is a hazard goes first.

questions.q: You stop at a stop sign where cross traffic does not have to stop. After stopping, when may you enter the intersection?
options: Right after stopping, because cross traffic must yield to you
When no vehicle on the cross street is close enough to be an immediate hazard
Only after waiting at least 10 seconds
questions.explain: After stopping, a driver must yield to cross traffic that is approaching closely enough to be an immediate hazard, then may proceed when it is reasonably safe.

questions.q: You arrive at an intersection controlled by this sign. What must you do?
options: Come to a full stop every time, even if the road is clear
Speed up to merge ahead of cross traffic
Slow down and give the right-of-way to vehicles in or close to the intersection, stopping if needed
questions.explain: At a yield sign you must give the right-of-way to vehicles already in the intersection or close enough to be an immediate hazard; you stop only when necessary.

questions.q: You are pulling out of a shopping center parking lot onto a public street. Who has the right-of-way?
options: Traffic on the street that is close enough to be a hazard
You do, once your front bumper is in the street
Whoever is driving the larger vehicle
questions.explain: A driver entering a street from private property or an alley must yield to all approaching traffic close enough to be an immediate hazard.

questions.q: Before you drive across a sidewalk to leave a driveway, a person is walking toward your path on the sidewalk. What should you do?
options: Yield to the person walking on the sidewalk
Honk so the person knows to stop
Drive across quickly before the person arrives
questions.explain: Before driving over a sidewalk, a driver must yield to any pedestrian approaching on it.

questions.q: A pedestrian is crossing in the crosswalk ahead of you (blue car). What must you do?
options: Drive around the pedestrian if there is room
Yield and let the pedestrian finish crossing safely
Honk so the pedestrian hurries
questions.explain: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing in a marked crosswalk and must slow down or take other action as needed to keep them safe.

questions.q: A pedestrian is crossing at a street corner where there are no painted crosswalk lines. Must you yield?
options: No, pedestrians only have the right-of-way in painted crosswalks
Only if a traffic signal is present
Yes, a corner crossing is an unmarked crosswalk and you must yield
questions.explain: The duty to yield covers pedestrians in marked crosswalks and in unmarked crosswalks at intersections.

questions.q: A car in the lane next to you has stopped at a crosswalk to let a pedestrian cross. What should you do?
options: Pass the stopped car carefully
Change lanes behind it and then pass
Do not pass the stopped car; stop and wait
questions.explain: When a vehicle has stopped at a crosswalk for a pedestrian, drivers coming from behind may not pass it, because the pedestrian may be hidden from view.

questions.q: A pedestrian is crossing in the middle of a block, away from any crosswalk. Which statement is correct?
options: The pedestrian should yield to nearby vehicles, but you must still use care to avoid hitting them
You may keep going at the same speed because the pedestrian is breaking the rule
The pedestrian always has the right-of-way, so you must stop in any lane
questions.explain: Outside a crosswalk a pedestrian must yield to vehicles close enough to be a hazard, but that does not remove a driver's duty to use due care for the pedestrian's safety.

questions.q: A pedestrian using a guide dog, or carrying a white cane (with or without a red tip), is about to cross in front of you. What must you do?
options: Give the pedestrian the right-of-way and take every needed precaution
Honk to warn the pedestrian
Drive past slowly, since the pedestrian cannot see you
questions.explain: California gives blind or partially blind pedestrians with a white cane or guide dog the right-of-way, and failing to yield to them is a misdemeanor.

questions.q: In California, failing to yield to a blind pedestrian who uses a white cane or guide dog is a misdemeanor with a fine of at least $___.
questions.explain: The law sets a fine of $500 to $1,000, jail of up to six months, or both, for failing to yield to a blind pedestrian.

questions.q: You stopped at a red light and want to turn right, and no sign prohibits it. Who must you yield to before turning?
options: Pedestrians in the nearby crosswalk and vehicles close enough to be a hazard
Only vehicles turning left from the opposite direction
No one, because a right turn on red is always allowed
questions.explain: After stopping, a right turn on red is allowed only while yielding to pedestrians in the adjacent crosswalk and to vehicles close enough to be an immediate hazard.

questions.q: Your light turns green, but a pedestrian is still in the crosswalk in front of you. What should you do?
options: Go, since the green light gives you the right-of-way
Wait until the pedestrian has crossed
Inch forward to signal the pedestrian to hurry
questions.explain: Even on a green light, drivers must yield to pedestrians and vehicles that are lawfully within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk.

questions.q: Your light is green, but traffic is backed up on the far side of the intersection and there is no room for your car. What should you do?
options: Enter and wait in the intersection until traffic moves
Enter only if you are turning
Wait behind the intersection until there is space for your car on the other side
questions.explain: California's anti-gridlock law forbids entering an intersection, even on green, unless there is room on the other side so you will not block cross traffic.

questions.q: Traffic ahead is stopped. Where should you avoid coming to a stop?
options: In a position that blocks a crosswalk
Behind the white stop line
A safe distance behind the car ahead
questions.explain: It is illegal to stop a vehicle unnecessarily in a way that blocks a marked or unmarked crosswalk or a sidewalk.

questions.q: An ambulance with its siren on and red lights flashing comes up behind you (blue car). What must you do?
options: Speed up to stay ahead of it
Stop right where you are in your lane
Drive to the right edge of the road and stop until it passes
questions.explain: When an emergency vehicle approaches with a siren and red light, drivers must yield, move to the right-hand edge or curb, stop, and stay stopped until it passes.

questions.q: You are in the middle of an intersection when you hear a siren and see a fire truck with red lights coming. What should you do?
options: Stop immediately inside the intersection
Back up out of the intersection
Continue through the intersection, then pull to the right and stop
questions.explain: The law says to pull to the right edge and stop clear of any intersection, so finish crossing first and then pull over.

questions.q: You are driving in a carpool (HOV) lane when an emergency vehicle with a siren and red light approaches. What should you do?
options: Stay in the carpool lane and slow down
Stop in the carpool lane
Leave the carpool lane as soon as you can do so safely
questions.explain: A driver in an exclusive or preferential use lane must exit that lane as soon as it can be done with reasonable safety when an emergency vehicle approaches.

questions.q: Unless you are driving an emergency vehicle, you may not follow a fire truck or ambulance that is responding to an emergency within ___ feet.
questions.explain: California forbids following within 300 feet of an emergency vehicle that is responding to an emergency.

questions.q: A police car with flashing lights is stopped on the right shoulder. You (blue car) are in the right lane of a multi-lane road. What should you do if the next lane is clear?
options: Move over one lane, away from the police car, when it is safe
Stay in your lane and keep your speed
Stop next to the police car
questions.explain: California's move-over law tells drivers to change into a lane not next to a stopped emergency vehicle when that is safe and practical.

questions.q: You are approaching a tow truck with flashing amber lights stopped on the shoulder, but heavy traffic makes changing lanes unsafe. What should you do?
options: Stay in your lane and slow to a safe speed while passing
Stop in your lane until the tow truck leaves
Pass on the shoulder on the other side
questions.explain: If moving over is unsafe or impractical, the move-over law requires you to slow to a reasonable and prudent speed for the conditions.

questions.q: As of January 1, 2026, California's move-over law also covers which of these stopped vehicles?
options: Any parked car with no lights on
Vehicles in a parking lot separated from the road by a barrier
Any stopped vehicle on the roadside showing hazard lights, cones, or flares
questions.explain: The law was expanded to include any stationary vehicle displaying hazard lights or warning devices such as cones, flares, or reflectors; it does not apply where a physical barrier separates the vehicle from the road.

questions.q: The school bus ahead of you (blue car) is stopped with red lights flashing and its stop arm out. What must you do?
options: Pass slowly on the left
Stop and stay stopped until the red lights stop flashing
Stop, then go once you see no children
questions.explain: Drivers must stop before passing a school bus that shows flashing red lights and a stop arm, and may not move past it until those signals turn off.

questions.q: You are on a divided highway. A school bus with flashing red lights is stopped on the other roadway, across the median. Must you stop?
options: No, you do not need to stop
Yes, all traffic must stop
Only if children are crossing toward you
questions.explain: On a divided highway, or a road with two or more lanes in each direction, you need not stop for a school bus on the other roadway.

questions.q: On a two-lane road, an oncoming school bus stops in front of you with red lights flashing and the stop arm out. What must you do?
options: Keep going, since the bus is in the other lane
Slow to 25 mph and pass
Stop until the red lights stop flashing
questions.explain: The school bus stop rule applies to drivers meeting the bus from either direction unless the road is divided or has two or more lanes each way.

questions.q: A school bus ahead of you turns on its flashing amber (yellow) lights. What does this usually mean?
options: The bus is about to stop to load or unload students
The bus is turning right
You may pass the bus quickly
questions.explain: School bus drivers turn on the amber warning lights as they approach a stop, beginning 200 feet before it, so expect the bus to stop and the red lights to come on.

questions.q: The railroad crossing gates are down and the lights are flashing. You (blue car) see no train yet. What should you do?
options: Drive around the gates carefully if no train is visible
Back up and cross at a different angle
Stay stopped until the gates go up and it is safe
questions.explain: It is illegal to drive through, around, or under a railroad crossing gate while it is closed.

questions.q: When a railroad crossing signal warns that a train is coming, you must stop at least ___ feet from the nearest rail.
questions.explain: Drivers must stop no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail when a signal, flagger, or nearby train warns of danger.

questions.q: Traffic is slow on the far side of a railroad crossing. When may you start across the tracks?
options: Only when there is room on the other side for your whole vehicle
As soon as the signals are off, even if you might stop on the tracks
Whenever the car ahead of you starts across
questions.explain: You may not enter a rail crossing, even with a signal to proceed, unless there is enough space on the other side for your vehicle.

questions.q: You are following a bus carrying passengers toward a railroad crossing with no train in sight. What should you expect?
options: The bus will speed up to cross quickly
The bus will stop before the tracks even if no train is coming
The bus will stop only if the gates are down
questions.explain: Buses carrying passengers, school buses with students, and trucks carrying certain hazardous materials generally must stop before the tracks and look and listen for trains.

questions.q: Buses carrying passengers must stop at railroad crossings no less than 15 feet and no more than ___ feet from the nearest rail.
questions.explain: These vehicles must stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail and look and listen in both directions before crossing.

questions.q: You (blue car) are at the yield line about to enter this roundabout. Who has the right-of-way?
options: Vehicles already circling in the roundabout
You, because you are entering
Whoever is on the right
questions.explain: Roundabouts use yield control at entry: vehicles already on the circular roadway may proceed, and entering drivers wait for a safe gap.

questions.q: In a roundabout in the United States, which direction does traffic travel around the center island?
options: Clockwise
Either direction, whichever is shorter
Counterclockwise
questions.explain: Traffic in a roundabout circulates counterclockwise, passing to the right of the center island.

questions.q: A funeral procession is being escorted by a uniformed peace officer who signals you to wait. What should you do?
options: Obey the officer and wait
Follow your green light instead of the officer
Join the end of the procession to get through
questions.explain: Ignoring the direction of a uniformed peace officer escorting a funeral procession is an infraction in California.

questions.q: On a steep, narrow mountain road, two cars meet and there is not enough room to pass. Which driver must yield?
options: The driver going uphill
The driver of the smaller car
The driver going downhill
questions.explain: When a grade is too narrow for vehicles to pass, the driver going downhill must yield and, if necessary, back up to a place where passing is possible.

questions.q: You see these lines in the center of a two-lane road. May you cross them to pass a slow car?
options: Yes, if no traffic is coming
Only during daylight hours
No, you may not drive to the left of these lines to pass
questions.explain: Double solid yellow lines prohibit driving to the left of them to pass in either direction.

questions.q: With these center lines, when may you cross them?
options: To pass a slow vehicle
Never, under any circumstances
To turn left into a driveway or at an intersection
questions.explain: Double yellow lines may be crossed to turn left at an intersection or into or out of a driveway or private road, or for a legal U-turn, but not to pass.

questions.q: Your car is in the lower-right lane. The solid yellow line is on your side of the center. May you pass the car ahead by crossing the center line?
options: No, passing is not allowed from your side
Yes, if the road ahead is clear
Yes, but only to pass a bicycle
questions.explain: When a solid and a broken yellow line are side by side, only drivers on the broken-line side may cross to pass; a solid line on your side means no passing.

questions.q: Your car is in the lower-right lane, and the broken yellow line is on your side of the center. What do these lines allow?
options: You may pass when the way ahead is clear and safe
Nothing; they mean no passing in both directions
Only oncoming traffic may pass
questions.explain: A driver on the side with the broken line may cross the double line to overtake and pass when it is safe.

questions.q: What does a single broken yellow center line on a two-lane road mean?
options: Traffic in both lanes moves the same direction
Passing is never allowed
Traffic moves in opposite directions, and passing with care is allowed in either direction when safe
questions.explain: A single broken yellow center line separates opposing traffic and marks a zone where drivers in either direction may pass with care.

questions.q: What does the broken white line between these two lanes mean?
options: Both lanes go the same direction, and you may change lanes when it is safe
The lanes carry traffic in opposite directions
You may never change lanes here
questions.explain: Broken white lane lines separate lanes moving in the same direction where crossing with care is allowed.

questions.q: Two lanes going the same direction are separated by a solid white line. What does this tell you?
options: Lane changes are encouraged here
Changing lanes across this line is discouraged
The left lane is for oncoming traffic
questions.explain: A solid white lane line is used where crossing between same-direction lanes is discouraged, such as near intersections and turn lanes.

questions.q: What is the center lane marked like this used for?
options: Passing slow traffic
Parking during rush hour
Left turns (and legal U-turns) by drivers from both directions
questions.explain: A two-way left-turn lane is set aside for vehicles making left turns in both directions; it is outlined by a solid outer and a broken inner yellow line.

questions.q: Traffic in your lane is moving slowly. May you drive in this center lane to get past it?
options: Yes, if the lane is empty
Yes, for up to half a mile
No, this lane is only for preparing to turn left or make a legal U-turn
questions.explain: A two-way left-turn lane may be used only when preparing for or making a left turn or legal U-turn, not for passing or through travel.

questions.q: The left lane is marked with white diamond symbols. What does this mean?
options: It is a high-occupancy vehicle (carpool) lane; follow the posted occupancy rules
It is a lane for trucks only
It is an emergency stopping lane
questions.explain: A white diamond marks a high-occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane, and drivers may use it only as allowed by the posted signs.

questions.q: On this divided road, what does the solid yellow line along the left side of your lanes mark?
options: A lane for oncoming traffic
A bike lane
The left edge of the roadway
questions.explain: On divided highways and one-way roads, a solid yellow line marks the left edge of the roadway; the right edge is marked in white.

questions.q: You must stop for a red light at this intersection. Where should you stop?
options: Behind the white stop line
In the crosswalk
Past the crosswalk, at the edge of the cross street
questions.explain: On a steady red signal, stop at the marked limit (stop) line, or before the crosswalk if there is no line.

questions.q: Which color of center line separates traffic moving in opposite directions?
questions.explain: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions; white lines separate lanes going the same way.

questions.q: What do double solid white lines between lanes mean?
options: You may cross them with care
You must not cross them
They mark the edge of a parking area
questions.explain: California law forbids crossing any part of double parallel solid white lines except in limited cases.

questions.q: A carpool (HOV) lane is separated from the other lanes by double solid lines. How may you enter or leave it?
options: Anywhere, as long as you signal
Only by crossing the lines at an exit ramp
Only at places marked for entry and exit, such as where a single broken line is used
questions.explain: You may not cross double solid lines next to an HOV lane; enter or exit only in designated areas or where a single broken line is in place.

questions.q: You may not drive in a two-way left-turn lane for more than ___ feet while preparing for and making a turn.
questions.explain: California limits travel in a two-way left-turn lane to 200 feet while preparing for and making the turn or merging out.

questions.q: Your turn signal must be on continuously during the last ___ feet before you turn.
questions.explain: A signal of intent to turn must be given continuously for the last 100 feet before the turn.

questions.q: You are giving a hand signal from the driver's window. Your arm is held straight out to the side. What does this mean?
options: Left turn
Right turn
Slowing or stopping
questions.explain: A hand and arm extended horizontally out of the left side of the vehicle signals a left turn.

questions.q: Which hand signal means you plan to turn right?
options: Left arm bent upward at the elbow
Left arm pointing straight down
Left arm straight out to the side
questions.explain: A right turn is signaled with the hand and arm extended upward outside the left side of the vehicle.

questions.q: Which hand signal tells drivers behind you that you are stopping or slowing suddenly?
options: Left arm straight out to the side
Left arm bent upward
Left arm extended downward
questions.explain: A hand and arm extended downward outside the vehicle signals a stop or sudden decrease in speed.

questions.q: Your turn signals stop working while you are driving. What does the law require when you need to signal?
options: Use hand and arm signals
Flash your headlights
Turn on your hazard lights before each turn
questions.explain: If signal lamps become inoperable while driving, the driver must use hand and arm signals instead.

questions.q: How should you make a right turn?
options: Swing wide into the left lane first
Start and finish the turn as close as practical to the right curb or edge
Turn from the center of the road
questions.explain: Both the approach and the right turn itself should be made as close as practicable to the right-hand curb or edge of the road.

questions.q: How should you make a left turn at an intersection on a two-way street?
options: Approach from the far-left lane, start turning inside the intersection, and finish in a legal lane
Start turning before you reach the intersection to save time
Approach from the right lane so you can see better
questions.explain: A left turn is approached from the far-left lawful lane, is not begun before entering the intersection, and must end in a lane open to your direction.

questions.q: You (blue car) want to turn right at the next corner, and a marked bike lane runs along the curb. What should you do?
options: Turn from your lane, crossing the bike lane at the corner
Wait until the cyclist is beside you, then turn
When it is safe, signal and move into the bike lane before turning
questions.explain: When you must cross an adjacent bike lane to turn, you should move into the bike lane before the turn, after checking that it is safe and signaling.

questions.q: You may drive in a bike lane to prepare for a turn only within ___ feet of the intersection.
questions.explain: Motor vehicles may use a bike lane to prepare for a turn only within 200 feet of the intersection, or to park or to enter or leave the road.

questions.q: When is passing another vehicle on the right allowed?
options: Any time you are in a hurry, using the shoulder
Never, under any circumstances
When the car ahead is turning left and there is room on the paved road
questions.explain: Passing on the right is allowed in limited cases, such as when the vehicle ahead is turning left, and never by driving off the paved roadway.

questions.q: On a two-lane road, you may not drive on the left side of the road to pass within ___ feet of an intersection or railroad crossing.
questions.explain: Driving on the left side of the road is not allowed within 100 feet of, or while crossing, an intersection or railroad grade crossing.

questions.q: Another driver is passing you on the left. What should you do?
options: Speed up so they finish passing quickly
Move left to block them
Keep to the right and do not speed up until they have passed
questions.explain: A driver being overtaken must move safely to the right and must not increase speed until the passing vehicle has fully passed.

questions.q: On a two-lane road where passing is unsafe, a slow vehicle with ___ or more vehicles lined up behind it must pull off at the nearest turnout or safe area.
questions.explain: A slow driver with five or more vehicles in line behind must use the nearest turnout or safe area to let them pass.

questions.q: In a business district, where may you make a U-turn?
options: At an intersection, or through an opening provided in a divided highway
Anywhere if no cars are coming
In the middle of the block
questions.explain: In a business district, U-turns are allowed only at intersections or at designated openings in a divided highway.

questions.q: In a residence district, you may not make a U-turn when another vehicle is approaching within 200 feet, unless:
options: You are at an intersection where a signal or sign controls the approaching vehicle
You signal first
You complete the turn quickly
questions.explain: A residential U-turn is not allowed with a vehicle approaching within 200 feet, except at an intersection where a traffic control device controls that vehicle.

questions.q: You want to make a U-turn at an intersection with a traffic light and no sign prohibiting it. Which lane must you turn from?
options: The right lane
Any lane, as long as you signal
The far-left lane available to your direction of travel
questions.explain: At a signal-controlled intersection, a U-turn may be made only from the far-left lane lawfully available to your direction of travel.

questions.q: You (blue car) are on the on-ramp and about to merge onto the freeway. What should you do?
options: Merge immediately; freeway traffic must make room for you
Signal and move into a freeway lane only when there is a safe gap
Stop at the end of the ramp and back up if no gap appears
questions.explain: You may change lanes only when it can be done with reasonable safety and after signaling, so look for a safe gap before merging.

questions.q: A freeway on-ramp has a traffic signal (ramp meter) showing red. What must you do?
options: Stop at the limit line and wait for green
Merge carefully without stopping
Ignore it if the freeway looks clear
questions.explain: Traffic signals at places other than intersections, including freeway on-ramps, must be obeyed; stop at the marked line or sign.

questions.q: Which curb color means no stopping, standing, or parking at any time?
questions.explain: A red curb bans stopping, standing, and parking, whether or not someone stays with the car. The only exception is a bus stopping in a red zone marked as a bus loading zone.

questions.q: Which curb color marks parking reserved for vehicles of disabled persons and disabled veterans?
questions.explain: Blue paint limits the space to vehicles of disabled persons and disabled veterans, which must show a disabled placard or special plate.

questions.q: Which curb color means you may park, but only for a limited time set by local rules?
questions.explain: A green curb allows time-limited parking. The time limit comes from the local ordinance and is usually posted.

questions.q: Which curb color allows you to stop only to load or unload passengers or freight?
questions.explain: Yellow means stop only long enough to load or unload people or goods, within any time limit set by local ordinance.

questions.q: Which curb color lets you stop just long enough to pick up or drop off passengers or drop a letter in a mailbox next to the curb?
questions.explain: A white curb is for brief passenger stops and for depositing mail in an adjacent mailbox.

questions.q: Which vehicle is allowed to stop at a red curb that is marked as a bus loading zone?
options: A taxi waiting for a fare
Any car whose driver stays behind the wheel
A bus
questions.explain: Red zones are off-limits to everyone, attended or not, except that a bus may stop where the red zone is marked or signed as a bus loading zone.

questions.q: When you park parallel to a curb, your right-hand wheels must be parallel to the curb and within ___ inches of it.
questions.explain: California law requires the right wheels to be parallel to the curb and no more than 18 inches away from it.

questions.q: How must a motorcycle be parked next to a curb?
options: With at least one wheel or fender touching the curb
Within 18 inches of the curb, like a car
At a 45-degree angle with the rear wheel toward the curb
questions.explain: Cars may be up to 18 inches from the curb, but a motorcycle must have at least one wheel or fender actually touching it.

questions.q: On a one-way street (not a divided highway), where may you park parallel to the curb?
options: Only on the right side
Only on the left side, so you face oncoming traffic
On either side, with the curbside wheels within 18 inches of that curb
questions.explain: On a one-way roadway you may park along the right curb or along the left curb, as long as the wheels next to the curb are parallel to it and within 18 inches.

questions.q: The car shown is parked facing uphill next to a curb. Is its front-wheel position correct?
options: No: the wheels should be pointed straight ahead
Yes: wheels turned away from the curb, with the car rolled back so a tire rests against the curb
No: the wheels should be turned toward the curb
questions.explain: Facing uphill, angle the front wheels away from the curb and let the car settle back so the rear of the front tire touches the curb; if the brakes slip, the curb stops the car. State law lets cities require wheels to be blocked against the curb on steep streets.
questions.source: CA DMV Driver Handbook § 6 (hill parking); Cal. Veh. Code § 22509

questions.q: The car shown is parked facing downhill next to a curb. Is its front-wheel position correct?
options: Yes: turning the wheels toward the curb lets the curb stop the car if it rolls
No: the wheels should be turned away from the curb
No: the wheels should be pointed straight ahead
questions.explain: Facing downhill, the front wheels should be turned into the curb so the curb catches the car if it starts to roll.
questions.source: CA DMV Driver Handbook § 6 (hill parking); Cal. Veh. Code § 22509

questions.q: You park on a hill where there is no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: To the left, toward the center of the road
Keep them straight
To the right, toward the edge of the road
questions.explain: With no curb to stop the car, turn the wheels right so that a rolling car heads off the road instead of into traffic.

questions.q: What must you do before leaving your car unattended on a street?
options: Lock the doors; nothing else is required
Set the parking brake and turn off the engine
Turn on the hazard lights and leave the engine running
questions.explain: The law forbids leaving a motor vehicle unattended on a highway unless its brakes are set and its engine is stopped.

questions.q: Cities may require drivers to block their wheels, such as by turning them against the curb, when leaving a car on a street with a grade steeper than ___ percent.
questions.explain: State law allows local authorities to require wheel blocking for unattended vehicles on grades over 3 percent in business and residence districts.

questions.q: You unhitch a trailer and leave it standing on a street. What does the law require?
options: Nothing, because a trailer has no engine
Leave it only next to a green curb
Set its brakes or block its wheels so it cannot move
questions.explain: A vehicle that is not a motor vehicle, such as a trailer, may not be left standing on a highway unless its brakes are set or its wheels are blocked to keep it from moving.

questions.q: Unless a local rule says otherwise, you may not park within ___ feet of a fire hydrant.
questions.explain: State law bans stopping or parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant unless a local ordinance sets a shorter distance or another exception applies.

questions.q: When may you stop for a moment within 15 feet of a fire hydrant?
options: When a licensed driver stays in the front seat and can move the car right away
When your hazard lights are on
When you will be gone less than 5 minutes
questions.explain: One exception to the hydrant rule is a car attended by a licensed driver sitting in the front seat who can move it immediately if needed.

questions.q: Do not stop or park within ___ feet of the driveway entrance to a fire station.
questions.explain: The law keeps the area within 15 feet of a fire station driveway clear, except for marked fire department vehicles.

questions.q: Unless a different distance is marked, you may not park within ___ feet of the approach side of a crosswalk.
questions.explain: Parking is banned within 20 feet of the side of a marked or unmarked crosswalk that traffic approaches from (15 feet where there is a curb extension), so drivers can see people crossing.

questions.q: Is it legal to double park (stop on the traffic side of a car already parked at the curb)?
options: No, except in narrow cases such as a school bus loading pupils in certain zones
Yes, if you stay in the car
Yes, for up to 5 minutes
questions.explain: Stopping or parking on the roadway side of a vehicle that is already at the curb is prohibited; the only exception is a school bus loading or unloading pupils on certain low-speed streets.

questions.q: Where is it illegal to stop or park unless traffic or an officer requires it?
options: At a green curb within the posted time
On the right side of a two-way street, 12 inches from the curb
Inside a tunnel
questions.explain: Stopping, standing, or parking in a tube or tunnel is prohibited for everyone except the crews maintaining it.

questions.q: Can you park across the front of a private driveway if you will be gone only a few minutes?
options: Yes, if your hazard lights are flashing
No, parking in front of a driveway is not allowed
Yes, if the driveway is not in use
questions.explain: Parking in front of a public or private driveway is prohibited no matter how short the stop; only authorized buses and taxis loading passengers are excepted.

questions.q: You park in a driveway, but the back of your car hangs over the sidewalk. Is this legal?
options: No, the car's body may not extend over any part of a sidewalk
Yes, because the tires are off the sidewalk
Yes, if pedestrians can still squeeze by
questions.explain: The law bans parking on a sidewalk or with the vehicle body extending over any part of it.

questions.q: A section of curb has been lowered so wheelchair users can reach the sidewalk. What does that mean for parking?
options: Small cars may park there
You may stop there to load for up to 3 minutes
You may not park in front of it or on it
questions.explain: No one may stop or park in front of or on a curb that has been lowered or cut down to give wheelchair users access to the sidewalk.

questions.q: Where the area next to a sidewalk access ramp is marked by a sign or red paint, you may not park within ___ feet of the ramp.
questions.explain: Keeping 3 feet clear around a marked sidewalk ramp lets wheelchair users reach it.

questions.q: A disabled parking space has a crosshatched (diagonal-striped) area beside it. Who may park in that striped area?
options: No one, not even a vehicle with a disabled placard
Only vehicles with a disabled placard or plate
Anyone, for up to 15 minutes
questions.explain: The striped space is kept open for loading wheelchairs and other access, so parking there is illegal for every vehicle, including placard holders.

questions.q: What must a vehicle show to park legally in a space designated for disabled persons?
options: A note on the dashboard explaining the stop
Hazard lights flashing
A disabled person placard or special disabled license plate
questions.explain: Only vehicles displaying a disabled person placard or the special identification plate may use these spaces; blocking access to them is also illegal.

questions.q: A driver with a valid disabled placard parks at a metered space on the street. Must they pay the meter?
options: Only half the meter fee is required
No, placard holders may park at meters without paying
Yes, the full meter fee always applies
questions.explain: California lets a disabled person or disabled veteran with a placard or special plate park at a metered space without paying the meter.

questions.q: A driver with a valid disabled placard parks at a green curb with a 1-hour limit. How long may they stay?
options: As long as they want; the posted time limit does not apply to them
Only 1 hour, like everyone else
Only 2 hours
questions.explain: Placard and special-plate holders may park for unlimited periods in zones with posted time limits, such as green zones, unless all parking there is banned.

questions.q: Your relative has a disabled person placard. May you use it to park in a disabled space while running errands alone?
options: Yes, if your relative gives permission
Yes, if the space is empty
No, it may be used only when you are transporting the disabled person
questions.explain: Lending a disabled placard is illegal; someone else may use it only while transporting the disabled person, and misuse carries a civil penalty of at least $250.

questions.q: In California, it is illegal for a driver age 21 or older to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ___ percent or more.
questions.explain: Driving with a BAC of 0.08% or higher is a crime by itself, even if the driver does not feel impaired.

questions.q: It is illegal to drive a commercial motor vehicle with a BAC of ___ percent or more.
questions.explain: Commercial drivers face a lower limit: 0.04% instead of the 0.08% that applies to ordinary drivers.

questions.q: A driver under 21 years old may not drive with a BAC of ___ percent or higher.
questions.explain: California has a near-zero limit for drivers under 21: a BAC of 0.01% or more, measured by a screening or chemical test, is a violation.

questions.q: Besides the 0.01 percent rule, it is a separate crime for a driver under 21 to drive with a BAC of ___ percent or more.
questions.explain: For drivers under 21, a BAC of 0.05% or more is a separate offense that is reported to the DMV as a conviction.

questions.q: What is the BAC limit for a driver who is carrying a paying passenger (for example, a ride-hire trip)?
options: 0.04 percent
0.08 percent
0.10 percent
questions.explain: When a passenger for hire is on board, driving with a BAC of 0.04% or more is illegal.

questions.q: Your BAC is 0.06 percent, but alcohol has clearly slowed your reactions. Can you be arrested for DUI?
options: No, only a BAC of 0.08% or more counts
No, unless you cause a crash
Yes, driving while under the influence of alcohol is illegal at any BAC
questions.explain: The law has two separate rules: one for a BAC of 0.08% or more and one for being under the influence of alcohol at all. You can break the second one below 0.08%.

questions.q: If a chemical test taken within ___ hours after driving shows 0.08 percent or more, the law presumes the driver was at that level while driving.
questions.explain: A test result of 0.08% or more within 3 hours after driving creates a presumption (which can be challenged) that the BAC was that high while driving.

questions.q: Your doctor prescribed a medicine that makes you drowsy. Which statement is true?
options: It is illegal to drive while under the influence of any drug, including a prescribed one
Prescribed medicine is always legal to take before driving
Only illegal drugs can lead to a DUI
questions.explain: The DUI law covers being under the influence of any drug, not just illegal ones.

questions.q: A driver charged with drug-impaired driving says the drug was legally prescribed to them. Is that a defense?
options: Yes, a valid prescription is a complete defense
Yes, if the driver shows the pill bottle
No, being legally allowed to use the drug is not a defense
questions.explain: California law states that being entitled to use a drug does not excuse driving under its influence.

questions.q: You had one beer and also took cold medicine. Neither alone would impair you, but together they do. Is it legal to drive?
options: Yes, if your BAC is under 0.08%
No, driving under the combined influence of alcohol and a drug is illegal
Yes, because each one alone is within limits
questions.explain: The law separately bans driving under the combined influence of alcohol and any drug.

questions.q: Under California law, may a person who is addicted to a drug drive a vehicle?
options: No, except while taking part in an approved narcotic treatment program
Yes, if they have not used the drug that day
Yes, if they are not carrying the drug
questions.explain: Driving while addicted to any drug is illegal; there is an exception for people in an approved narcotic treatment program.

questions.q: What does California's implied consent law mean?
options: You must agree to a vehicle search at any traffic stop
An officer needs your written permission before any test
By driving, you have agreed to a blood or breath test if lawfully arrested for DUI
questions.explain: Anyone who drives in California is treated as having already consented to chemical testing of blood or breath for alcohol after a lawful DUI arrest.

questions.q: You are lawfully arrested for driving under the influence of alcohol. Who chooses whether the test is of your blood or your breath?
options: A judge decides later
You do, and the officer must tell you that you have the choice
The officer always decides
questions.explain: For an alcohol DUI arrest, the driver chooses between a blood test and a breath test, and the officer must explain that choice.

questions.q: After a DUI arrest, do you have the right to talk to a lawyer before deciding whether to take a chemical test?
options: No, you have no right to a lawyer before deciding or during the test
Yes, the test must wait until your lawyer arrives
Yes, but only for a blood test
questions.explain: The officer must tell you there is no right to have a lawyer present before choosing or taking the test, and that a refusal can be used against you in court.

questions.q: An adult driver refuses a chemical test after a lawful DUI arrest, with no prior DUI offenses. What happens to the driving privilege?
options: It is suspended for 30 days
Nothing, because refusing is your right
It is suspended for one year
questions.explain: Refusing or failing to complete the required test leads to a one-year suspension by the DMV for a first refusal.

questions.q: If a driver refuses a chemical test within 10 years of a prior DUI conviction, the DMV revokes the driving privilege for ___ years.
questions.explain: If a refusal happens within 10 years of a prior DUI conviction or DUI-related DMV suspension, the DMV revokes the privilege for two years; with two or more priors, three years.

questions.q: Can your refusal to take a chemical test after a DUI arrest be used against you in court?
options: Yes, the refusal may be used as evidence
No, it can never be mentioned
Only if you also failed a field sobriety test
questions.explain: Part of the required warning is that a refusal may be used against the driver in a court of law.

questions.q: An adult driver takes a roadside preliminary alcohol screening (PAS) breath test. Does that replace the chemical test required after a DUI arrest?
options: Yes, it counts as the chemical test
Yes, if the PAS result is under 0.08%
No, the PAS test does not satisfy the chemical test requirement
questions.explain: The PAS is an investigative field test. The officer must explain that taking it does not meet the obligation to take a blood, breath, or urine test after arrest, and that an adult may refuse the PAS itself.

questions.q: When an officer takes your license after a DUI arrest, the notice of suspension acts as a temporary license that is valid for ___ days from the arrest.
questions.explain: The officer keeps your California license and gives you a notice that also serves as a temporary license for 30 days from the date of arrest.

questions.q: To get a DMV hearing before your DUI-related suspension takes effect, you must request it within ___ days of receiving the notice.
questions.explain: A hearing request made within 10 days of receiving the notice entitles you to a hearing before the suspension starts.

questions.q: After a DUI arrest with a BAC of 0.08% or more, the DMV suspends your license. How does this relate to the criminal court case?
options: It happens only after you are convicted in court
It replaces the criminal case
It is a separate civil action that happens regardless of the court case
questions.explain: The DMV's administrative suspension is a civil matter, independent of whether the driver is found guilty in criminal court.

questions.q: An adult driver with no prior DUI record is caught driving with a BAC of 0.08% or more. How long is the DMV's administrative suspension?
options: Three years
Four months
Ten days
questions.explain: With no prior offenses in the past 10 years, the DMV's administrative suspension for driving at 0.08% or more lasts four months.

questions.q: A 19-year-old driver is found driving with a BAC of 0.02 percent. What is the shortest DMV suspension that can apply?
options: One year
30 days
No suspension, because the BAC is under 0.05%
questions.explain: A driver under 21 who violates the 0.01% rule faces a DMV suspension of at least one year.

questions.q: A driver under 21 who is lawfully stopped refuses a preliminary alcohol screening test. What is the result?
options: A warning only
A fine, with no effect on the license
The driving privilege is suspended or revoked for one to three years
questions.explain: Drivers under 21 are treated as having consented to a screening test. Refusing leads to a suspension or revocation of one to three years, depending on prior offenses.

questions.q: A 16-year-old without a license yet is convicted of a DUI-type offense. What does the court order?
options: A fine only
A delay of one year, counted from when they become eligible to drive
No penalty, because they have no license
questions.explain: When an unlicensed person under 21 is convicted, the court orders the DMV to delay issuing a license for one year after the person becomes eligible.

questions.q: A person on probation for DUI may not drive with a BAC of what level or higher?
options: 0.01 percent
0.05 percent
0.08 percent
questions.explain: Drivers on probation for DUI face the same near-zero 0.01% limit that applies to drivers under 21.

questions.q: You are driving on a highway. May your adult passenger drink a beer?
options: Yes, if the passenger is 21 or older
Yes, if the driver is not drinking
No, passengers may not drink alcohol in a moving vehicle on a highway
questions.explain: The law bans drinking alcohol by the driver while driving and by any passenger in a vehicle being driven on a highway.

questions.q: Is it legal for a driver to carry an opened can of beer on their person while driving?
options: Yes, if the can is less than half full
No, a driver may not possess an opened alcohol container while driving
Yes, if the driver does not drink from it
questions.explain: A driver may not have an opened container of alcohol, or one with a broken seal or some contents removed, in their possession while driving.

questions.q: May a passenger hold an opened bottle of wine in a car traveling on a highway?
options: No, passengers may not possess opened alcohol containers either
Yes, only the driver is restricted
Yes, if the bottle has been recorked
questions.explain: The open container rule applies to passengers too, not just the driver.

questions.q: You are bringing home a partly finished bottle of wine from a restaurant. Where should you keep it while driving?
options: Behind the driver's seat
In the glove compartment
In the trunk
questions.explain: An opened alcohol container must be kept in the trunk. If the vehicle has no trunk, it must go in an area not normally occupied by the driver or passengers.

questions.q: Your vehicle has no trunk. Where may you keep an opened container of alcohol while driving?
options: Under the passenger seat
In an area that the driver and passengers do not normally occupy
In the glove compartment
questions.explain: Without a trunk, the container must go in an area not normally occupied by people, and the law says the glove compartment and utility compartments do not count.

questions.q: Where in a vehicle do the open container rules NOT apply?
options: The living quarters of a motorhome or camper
The back seat of a sedan
The bed of a pickup truck
questions.explain: The ban on keeping opened alcohol in the passenger area does not apply to the living quarters of a housecar or camper.

questions.q: An 18-year-old is driving alone with a sealed case of beer in the car. Which is true?
options: It is legal because the beer is sealed
It is legal if the beer is in the trunk
It is illegal unless they are with a parent or other allowed adult, or carrying it for work
questions.explain: Drivers under 21 may not knowingly carry alcohol, even sealed, unless accompanied by a parent, guardian, responsible adult relative, or adult designated by the parent, or carrying it as part of a job with a licensed alcohol business.

questions.q: If a driver under 21 illegally carries alcohol in a car registered to them, the car may be impounded for up to ___ days for each violation.
questions.explain: The vehicle may be impounded at the owner's expense for 1 to 30 days per violation.

questions.q: While driving, where may you keep an opened package of cannabis?
options: In the trunk
In the center console
