On the passenger seat
questions.explain: Having an opened cannabis container or loose cannabis flower while driving is an infraction unless it is in the trunk.

questions.q: It is a cloudy afternoon and rain is heavy enough that your wipers must run nonstop. What does California law require?
options: Turn on your headlights
Turn on only your parking lights
Turn on your hazard flashers
questions.explain: California treats weather that keeps your wipers in continuous use as inclement weather, and in inclement weather you must drive with your headlights on.

questions.q: Under California law, darkness (when headlights are required) begins ___ minutes after sunset.
questions.explain: The Vehicle Code defines darkness as starting one-half hour after sunset and lasting until one-half hour before sunrise.

questions.q: Weather counts as inclement (headlights required) when it keeps you from clearly seeing a person or vehicle on the road ___ feet away.
questions.explain: If fog, smoke or similar conditions keep you from clearly seeing people or vehicles 1,000 feet ahead, you must use your headlights.

questions.q: At night you must switch from high beams to low beams when an oncoming vehicle is within ___ feet.
questions.explain: Within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle you must aim your lights so the glare does not hit the other driver's eyes; low beams do that.

questions.q: At night you must use low beams when you are following another vehicle within ___ feet.
questions.explain: When you are within 300 feet behind another vehicle, the law requires your lowest beam so you do not blind the driver through the mirrors.

questions.q: When may you drive with only your parking lights on?
options: At dusk, before full darkness
In light fog during the day
Never; parking lights may be on while driving only if the headlights are also on
questions.explain: California does not allow driving with parking lamps alone; they may be lit while moving only together with headlights (or when working as turn signals).

questions.q: An adult driver wants to use a phone while driving. Which is legal in California?
options: Talking on the phone in hands-free, voice-operated mode
Holding the phone to your ear at a red light
Typing a text message while driving slowly
questions.explain: Drivers may not hold and operate a phone while driving; adults may use one only if it is set up for voice-operated, hands-free use.

questions.q: Your phone is mounted on the dashboard where it does not block your view. How may you touch it while driving?
options: To type a short address into the map
Any way you like, as long as it stays in the mount
With a single swipe or tap of one finger to turn a feature on or off
questions.explain: A mounted phone may be touched only for a single swipe or tap to activate or deactivate a function; longer handling is not allowed.

questions.q: You are driving and see a serious crash. May you use your handheld phone to call 911?
options: No, you must first pull over and turn off the engine
Yes, calls for emergency purposes are allowed
Only if a passenger cannot make the call
questions.explain: California's hands-free rule does not apply to calls made for emergency purposes, such as calling police, fire or medical help.

questions.q: Who must wear a seat belt in a passenger car in California?
options: The driver and every passenger 16 or older (younger children need a child seat or belt under the child-passenger laws)
Only the driver and front-seat passenger
Only people riding on freeways
questions.explain: The driver may not operate the car unless the driver and all passengers 16 and older are properly belted; younger riders are covered by the child restraint laws.

questions.q: A 17-year-old passenger refuses to buckle up. Who can be cited?
options: Only the driver
Only the vehicle's registered owner
Both the driver and the passenger
questions.explain: The driver must not drive with unbelted passengers 16 or older, and a passenger 16 or older is also personally required to be belted.

questions.q: In general, a child under ___ years old must ride in the rear seat in an approved child passenger restraint.
questions.explain: California requires children under 8 to be secured in a rear seat in a child restraint that meets federal safety standards, with limited exceptions.

questions.q: A child under 2 years old must ride in a rear-facing child seat unless the child:
options: Weighs at least 40 pounds or is at least 40 inches tall
Is riding on a short trip
Is sitting next to a parent in the back seat
questions.explain: Children under 2 must be rear-facing unless they already weigh 40 pounds or more or are 40 inches or taller.

questions.q: A 7-year-old is 4 feet 10 inches tall. What does California law allow?
options: The child must still use a booster seat until age 8
The child may ride unbelted in the back seat
The child may use a properly fitted safety belt instead of a child seat
questions.explain: A child under 8 who is at least 4 feet 9 inches tall may be properly restrained by a safety belt rather than a child restraint system.

questions.q: Where must you never place a rear-facing child seat?
options: Behind the driver's seat
In a front seat that has an active passenger air bag
In the middle of the back seat
questions.explain: The law forbids putting a rear-facing child seat in a front seat with an active frontal passenger air bag, because a deploying air bag can strike the seat.

questions.q: You are driving a 12-year-old to school. What must the child use?
options: A safety belt or an appropriate child restraint
Nothing, if riding in the back seat
A safety belt only on freeways
questions.explain: Children who are 8 or older but under 16 must be secured in a child restraint or by a safety belt.

questions.q: A child ___ years old or younger may not be left alone in a car when there is a significant risk to the child's health or safety, or when the engine is running or the keys are in the ignition.
questions.explain: California forbids leaving a child 6 or younger in a vehicle without supervision under those conditions.

questions.q: To avoid violating California's unattended-child law, a young child left in a car must be supervised by someone at least ___ years old.
questions.explain: The law requires supervision by a person who is 12 or older when a child 6 or younger is in the vehicle.

questions.q: Why should you never leave a child alone in a parked car, even for a minute?
options: Children cool down faster than adults in parked cars
Cracking a window keeps the car cool enough
A child's body heats up three to five times faster than an adult's
questions.explain: NHTSA warns that a child's temperature rises much faster than an adult's, and opening windows or parking in shade does little to cool the car.

questions.q: How close may you follow another vehicle?
options: No closer than is reasonable and prudent for the speed, traffic and road conditions
As close as you like if your brakes are good
Exactly one car length at any speed
questions.explain: California bans following more closely than is reasonable and prudent, considering speed, traffic and the road surface.

questions.q: Is it legal to toss a cigarette butt out of your car window?
options: Yes, if the cigarette is put out
Yes, on private roads
No, throwing any lit or unlit cigarette onto a road or nearby area is illegal
questions.explain: California bans throwing lighted or unlighted cigarettes, cigars, matches or anything burning from a vehicle onto a road or the area next to it.

questions.q: A passenger throws an empty bottle onto the highway. What is true?
options: It is legal if the bottle is plastic
Throwing bottles, cans or trash onto a highway is illegal
It is legal on rural roads
questions.explain: The Vehicle Code forbids throwing or depositing bottles, cans, garbage, glass or anything likely to damage traffic onto a highway.

questions.q: Which is legal while driving a car in California?
options: Wearing an earbud in one ear only
Wearing earbuds in both ears
Wearing a headset that covers both ears
questions.explain: Drivers and bicyclists may not wear earphones, earplugs or a headset in or over both ears; one ear must stay uncovered.

questions.q: When may you move from one lane to another?
options: Any time there is a gap of one car length
Right after signaling, even if a car is beside you
Only when the move can be made with reasonable safety, after signaling if others may be affected
questions.explain: Turning or moving left or right is allowed only when it is reasonably safe, and you must signal if any other vehicle could be affected.

questions.q: You are involved in a crash in which someone is injured. What must you do?
options: Stop immediately, exchange information and give reasonable help to the injured
Leave if it was not your fault
Drive to the nearest police station before stopping
questions.explain: Drivers in an injury or fatal crash must stop at the scene at once, share identifying information and give reasonable aid, such as arranging transport to medical care.

questions.q: You back into a parked, empty car and dent it. You cannot find the owner. What must you do?
options: Drive away since nobody saw it
Wait 10 minutes and then leave
Leave a note with your name and address on the car and notify police or CHP
questions.explain: For property-only damage when the owner cannot be found, leave a written notice in an obvious place on the vehicle and promptly notify the local police or CHP.

questions.q: If a crash injures or kills someone, the driver must file a written report with CHP or the city police within ___ hours.
questions.explain: California requires a written report to the Highway Patrol or the city police department within 24 hours of an injury or fatal crash.

questions.q: When passing a bicycle going the same direction, you must leave at least ___ feet between your vehicle and the bicycle or rider.
questions.explain: California's Three Feet for Safety Act forbids passing a bicycle with less than three feet between any part of your vehicle and the bicycle or its rider.

questions.q: Traffic and a narrow road make it impossible to give a bicyclist 3 feet. What should you do?
options: Pass quickly to reduce the time beside the rider
Slow down and pass only when it will not endanger the bicyclist
Honk so the rider moves off the road
questions.explain: If you cannot leave three feet, you must slow to a reasonable speed and pass only when doing so would not put the rider at risk.

questions.q: You are on a road with two lanes in your direction and a bicyclist is in your lane. Before passing, what must you do if it is safe and legal?
options: Change into the other lane
Pass within your own lane
Follow the bicyclist until the road ends
questions.explain: When another lane going your way is available, California requires you to move into it, if practicable and legal, before passing a bicyclist in your lane.

questions.q: You plan to turn right and a bike lane is next to your lane. How should you make the turn?
options: Turn from your lane, crossing the bike lane at the corner
Speed up to turn before the bicyclist arrives
Check for bicyclists, merge into the bike lane close to the corner, then turn
questions.explain: To turn across an adjacent bike lane, you must first move into the bike lane (no more than 200 feet before the intersection) and then turn from there.

questions.q: What rights does a bicyclist riding on a California road have?
options: The same rights and duties as a driver, except rules that cannot apply to bikes
No right to use a traffic lane
Only the rights of a pedestrian
questions.explain: People riding bicycles on a highway have all the rights and are subject to the same rules as vehicle drivers, except provisions that by nature cannot apply.

questions.q: What does California law call a two-wheeled motorcycle traveling between rows of stopped or moving vehicles in the same lane?
options: Lane sharing
Tailgating
Lane splitting
questions.explain: California defines lane splitting as riding a two-wheeled motorcycle between rows of vehicles in the same lane, and lets CHP publish safety guidelines on it.

questions.q: Who must wear a helmet on a motorcycle in California?
options: Only riders under 18
Both the rider and any passenger
Only the rider, not the passenger
questions.explain: California requires the motorcycle driver and every passenger to wear a properly fastened, approved safety helmet.

questions.q: On a highway with no special truck lanes posted, where must slower vehicles such as large trucks drive?
options: In the right-hand lane or as close as practical to the right edge
In the far left lane
In any lane they choose
questions.explain: Vehicles covered by the 55 mph limit must use designated lanes when signed, and otherwise keep to the right-hand lane (with some exceptions on wide divided highways).

questions.q: Can a friend ride in the open bed of your pickup truck on a highway?
options: Yes, if they sit down
Yes, if you stay under 25 mph
No, unless the person is secured with an approved restraint system
questions.explain: California forbids carrying people in the back of a pickup or flatbed on a highway unless they are secured by a restraint that meets federal standards (with narrow farm, parade and emergency exceptions).

questions.q: Which screen may be on and visible to you while you drive?
options: A GPS map display
A movie playing on a dash screen
A video streaming on a phone
questions.explain: Video or TV screens may not operate where the driver can see them, but navigation, mapping and vehicle information displays are allowed.

questions.q: When should you use your horn?
options: To greet a friend on the sidewalk
To tell a slow driver to hurry up
When reasonably necessary to warn others for safety
questions.explain: The horn is to be used as an audible warning when reasonably needed for safe operation, not for other purposes.

questions.q: You parked on a busy street. When may you open your door on the traffic side?
options: Any time, since moving drivers must avoid you
Only when it is reasonably safe and will not interfere with traffic
Only when your hazard lights are on
questions.explain: You may not open a door on the traffic side unless it can be done safely without interfering with traffic, and you should not leave it open longer than needed.

questions.q: According to NHTSA, sending or reading a text takes your eyes off the road for about 5 seconds. At 55 mph, that is like:
options: Driving the length of a football field blindfolded
Driving about one car length
Driving one mile
questions.explain: NHTSA compares a 5-second glance at a text at 55 mph to covering a football field's length with your eyes closed.

questions.q: According to NHTSA, when are drowsy-driving crashes most common?
options: Between 8 a.m. and noon
Right after eating breakfast
Between midnight and 6 a.m., and in the late afternoon
questions.explain: NHTSA notes that drowsy crashes cluster from midnight to 6 a.m. and in the late afternoon, when the body's internal clock dips.

questions.q: According to NHTSA, where should children under 13 ride?
options: In the back seat
In the front passenger seat
Anywhere, as long as air bags are on
questions.explain: NHTSA advises seating children under 13 in the back seat to keep them away from deploying frontal air bags.

questions.q: How should a shoulder belt be worn?
options: Behind your back
Under your arm
Across the middle of the chest, away from the neck
questions.explain: NHTSA says the shoulder belt goes across the middle of the chest and away from the neck, never behind the back or under an arm.

questions.q: May a friend ride in the trunk of your car for a short trip?
options: Yes, if the trunk lid is open
No, riding in a trunk is illegal
Yes, if the trip is under one mile
questions.explain: California forbids riding in a vehicle's trunk and forbids drivers from knowingly allowing it.

questions.q: A teen who has finished (or is enrolled in) driver education may apply for an instruction permit at what minimum age?
options: 15 years and 6 months
15 years
16 years
questions.explain: California may issue an instruction permit at 15½ to an applicant who has completed driver education and is taking or enrolled in driver training.

questions.q: A minor must hold an instruction permit for at least ___ months before applying for a provisional license.
questions.explain: The provisional licensing program requires holding a permit for no less than six months before applying.

questions.q: Before getting a provisional license, a minor must complete ___ hours of supervised driving practice.
questions.explain: Teens need 50 hours of supervised practice, certified by a parent, guardian, spouse or instructor, on top of required driver training.

questions.q: At least ___ of a teen's required supervised practice hours must be driven at night (during darkness).
questions.explain: At least 10 of the 50 practice hours must take place during darkness.

questions.q: A minor with an instruction permit may practice with a California-licensed driver who is at least ___ years old (unless that driver is a parent, guardian, spouse or licensed instructor).
questions.explain: The supervising driver for a minor permit holder must be 25 or older, unless it is the teen's parent, spouse, guardian or a licensed or certified instructor.

questions.q: A minor fails the DMV written test. How long must they wait before retaking it?
options: At least one day
At least one month
At least one week
questions.explain: Under the provisional program, a minor must wait no less than one week after failing the written test and two weeks after failing the driving test.

questions.q: A minor fails the DMV driving test. How long must they wait before retaking it?
options: At least two weeks
At least two days
At least six months
questions.explain: The law sets a minimum two-week wait after a failed driving test for provisional applicants.

questions.q: During the first year of a provisional license, when may the teen NOT drive unless accompanied by a parent, guardian, licensed driver 25 or older, or instructor (with limited exceptions)?
options: Between 9 p.m. and 6 a.m.
Between midnight and 4 a.m.
Between 11 p.m. and 5 a.m.
questions.explain: For the first 12 months, a provisional licensee may not drive from 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. without a qualifying adult unless an exception such as school, work or medical need applies.

questions.q: During the first year, a provisional licensee may not carry passengers under ___ years old unless accompanied by a qualifying adult.
questions.explain: For the first 12 months, provisional drivers may not transport passengers younger than 20 without a parent, guardian, licensed driver 25 or older, or instructor.

questions.q: The night-driving and passenger restrictions on a provisional license apply for the first ___ months.
questions.explain: The restrictions last for the first 12 months after the provisional license is issued.

questions.q: A provisional licensee in the first year must drive alone at 6 a.m. to a job because no other transportation works. What is needed?
options: Nothing; jobs are always exempt
A signed note from the employer confirming the job and its expected end date
A note from any adult friend
questions.explain: The employment exception requires the teen to carry a signed employer statement verifying the job and the probable date it will end.

questions.q: May a police officer stop a car only to check whether a teen driver is obeying provisional license restrictions?
options: No, that alone is not a valid reason for a stop
Yes, at any time
Yes, but only after 11 p.m.
questions.explain: The law says officers may not stop a vehicle for the sole purpose of checking provisional license restrictions.

questions.q: A provisional driver gets 2 violation points within 12 months. What happens?
options: A warning letter only
Immediate one-year suspension
A 30-day restriction requiring a licensed adult 25 or older (or parent/guardian) in the car
questions.explain: Two or more points in 12 months triggers a 30-day restriction during which the teen must be accompanied by a parent, spouse, guardian or licensed driver 25 or older.

questions.q: A provisional driver gets 3 violation points within 12 months. What is the penalty?
options: A 6-month suspension and one year of probation
A 30-day restriction
A fine only
questions.explain: Three or more points in 12 months leads to a six-month suspension plus a one-year probation term.

questions.q: What words appear on a California driver license issued to someone under 18?
options: "Learner"
"Restricted to daytime"
"Provisional until age 18"
questions.explain: A license for a person under 18 must display the words "provisional until age 18."

questions.q: A 17-year-old driver wants to take a call using a hands-free headset. Is that legal?
options: Yes, hands-free use is legal for everyone
No, drivers under 18 may not use a phone even hands-free
Yes, but only on surface streets
questions.explain: Drivers under 18 may not use a wireless phone or electronic communications device while driving, even with hands-free equipment.

questions.q: After moving, you must notify the DMV of your new address within ___ days.
questions.explain: A licensed driver who moves or gets a new mailing address must tell the DMV the old and new addresses within 10 days.

questions.q: What must you have with you whenever you drive?
options: Your valid driver license
Your birth certificate
Your vehicle's title
questions.explain: Licensees must keep their valid driver license in their immediate possession whenever they drive on a highway and show it to a peace officer on request.

questions.q: If you are in a crash with injury, death, or property damage over $1,000, you must report it to the DMV (form SR-1) within ___ days.
questions.explain: The driver must report a qualifying collision to the DMV within 10 days, personally or through an insurance agent, broker or legal representative.

questions.q: A DMV crash report (SR-1) is required when property damage to any one person is more than $___.
questions.explain: The DMV report is required when damage to any one person's property exceeds $1,000, or anyone is injured or killed.

questions.q: You are in a crash where a passenger in the other car is slightly hurt but damage is only $400. Must you file an SR-1 with the DMV?
options: No, damage is under $1,000
Only if police were called
Yes, any injury makes the report required
questions.explain: An SR-1 is required for any bodily injury or death, no matter how small the property damage is.

questions.q: What can happen if you fail to file a required SR-1 crash report?
options: The DMV will suspend your driving privilege
Nothing, the report is optional
Your vehicle registration is transferred
questions.explain: The DMV must suspend the driving privilege of anyone who fails to make a required accident report until the report or proof of insurance is received.

questions.q: What proof of insurance must be in your vehicle?
options: Your insurance policy's full contract
Nothing; the DMV keeps it on file
Evidence of the financial responsibility (such as an insurance card) in effect for the vehicle
questions.explain: Drivers and owners must be able to show financial responsibility at all times and keep evidence of it in the vehicle.

questions.q: An officer asks for proof of insurance after a traffic stop. Can you show it on your phone?
options: No, only a paper card is accepted
Yes, electronic proof on a mobile device is allowed
Only if the officer agrees in writing
questions.explain: California lets drivers show evidence of financial responsibility on a mobile electronic device, and the officer may view only that information.

questions.q: For policies issued or renewed since January 1, 2025, minimum liability insurance in California must cover at least $___,000 for injury or death of one person.
questions.explain: The minimum bodily injury limit is now $30,000 per person for policies issued or renewed on or after January 1, 2025.

questions.q: For policies issued or renewed since January 1, 2025, minimum liability insurance must cover at least $___,000 for injury or death of two or more people in one crash.
questions.explain: The minimum is $60,000 for injury or death of all persons in one accident under the 2025 limits.

questions.q: For policies issued or renewed since January 1, 2025, minimum liability insurance must cover at least $___,000 for property damage.
questions.explain: Property damage coverage must be at least $15,000 per accident under the limits that took effect January 1, 2025.

questions.q: You are in a reportable crash and had no insurance. What will the DMV do?
options: Suspend your driving privilege
Issue a warning only
Require a new vision test
questions.explain: When a driver in a reportable accident lacked financial responsibility, the DMV must suspend the driving privilege after giving notice.

questions.q: A basic Class C license lets you drive which vehicle?
options: Any vehicle with three or more axles
A two-wheel motorcycle
A two-axle vehicle with a gross vehicle weight rating of 26,000 pounds or less
questions.explain: Class C covers two-axle vehicles rated at 26,000 pounds or less (with some towing limits), and does not include two-wheel motorcycles.

questions.q: Which license class do you need to ride a two-wheel motorcycle?
options: Class M1
Class C
Class B
questions.explain: A two-wheel motorcycle requires a Class M1 license or an M1 endorsement on another license.

questions.q: A person under 21 wants a motorcycle license. What must they complete?
options: A 50-hour supervised practice log
Nothing beyond the Class C test
A novice motorcycle safety training program
questions.explain: Applicants under 21 cannot get a Class M1 or M2 license or endorsement without proof of completing a novice motorcycle safety training program.

questions.q: A driver is presumed to be a negligent operator with ___ or more points in 12 months.
questions.explain: The negligent operator thresholds are 4 points in 12 months, 6 in 24 months, or 8 in 36 months.

questions.q: How many points does a DUI or hit-and-run conviction add to a California driving record?
options: 1 point
2 points
4 points
questions.explain: Convictions for hit-and-run, DUI and reckless driving each count as two points; most other moving violations count as one.

questions.q: You are found responsible for a traffic collision. How many points are added to your record?
options: 1 point
0 points
3 points
questions.explain: A collision in which the DMV deems the driver responsible counts as one point.

questions.q: When does an original California driver license expire?
options: On your third birthday after you applied
Ten years after the date you applied
On your fifth birthday after the date you applied
questions.explain: An original license expires on the applicant's fifth birthday following the application date.
